fix.summary: At exact HEAD f69c26dd4d83f73f6cd80829c12fa2d7c5b877f6, amendment 003 is not yet contract-complete. The capacity trigger is materially supported without reading archived payloads (the 1f8071d tree contains about 417.17 MB under `.ak/dockets`, overwhelmingly JSONL), and the converged prior authority remains governing except where expressly superseded. Four authority-level defects remain. (1) The amendment simultaneously forbids copying Git-recoverable content even when it reappears in model/tool output and requires an admitted raw stream, stored only as compressed members/chunks, to reconstruct the sanitized canonical bytes exactly. A session containing a `read` of a tracked file cannot satisfy both. Preserve the owner’s Git-reference-only rule by defining a single reference-aware logical reconstruction contract (including framing/encoding and reference-resolution failure), or declare such a stream inadmissible; do not silently create a raw-session exception or permit lossy filtering. (2) The Git-reference lifecycle is circular for newly created canonical decision artifacts: a manifest cannot contain the full SHA of the commit that will contain that manifest/artifact, and the Recorder is forbidden to commit. Distinguish already-committed, mechanically verified objects eligible for repository/full-commit/path/blob/SHA-256 references from new canonical artifacts, and freeze a non-circular forward sealing lifecycle that stores each new artifact once without allowing dirty bytes to masquerade as a Git reference. (3) Caller-owned admission lacks temporal and ownership semantics. The failure-diagnosis reason may only become known after the one exact child command exits, while default scratch must be deleted; the contract does not say when or how the caller decides before irreversible deletion, what happens when no valid decision arrives, or how this avoids retry/second-spawn and indefinite raw retention. Freeze that lifecycle and state that the caller—not the Recorder or model—owns required-exhibit selection and every ambiguity/non-promotion disposition. (4) A disposition must not excuse omission of mandatory authority/task/input bytes or evidence required for the decision chain; tighten the current 'archive fails or records a non-promotion disposition as allowed' language accordingly. State that admission reasons and Git coordinates are provenance assertions, that references are verified against exact bytes at admission but do not prove truth/authenticity/future availability, and that admission/reference/reconstruction/compression failures obey the already-frozen Recorder-infrastructure precedence, cleanup, atomic-promotion, and no-Receipt-synthesis law. These are contract/state/trust decisions, not requests for implementation proof or fixtures.
